## Analysis

I computed space groups, connectivity/dimensionality, and bond‑direction + bond‑polarizability tensors (Lorentz–Lorenz, anisotropic anion model) for all 100 structures. Birefringence is governed by (i) the intrinsic polarizability anisotropy of the building unit and (ii) whether those units are **parallel‑aligned** (no cancellation), plus (iii) high polarizability density (heavy, soft anions; lone pairs).

**Key structural findings:**

| ID | Compound | Motif found | Alignment order param. |
|---|---|---|---|
| c062 | Cs₃[BPAs] (Cc) | **linear** P=B=As triatomic anion (P–B 1.77, B–As 1.90 Å, ∠178°), isolated in Cs⁺ matrix | bond‑direction tensor = **[0, 0, 1]** — perfect |
| c089 | Cs₂Se₃ (Cmc2₁) | bent **Se₃²⁻** trimers (Se–Se 2.40 Å, ∠106°), homopolar chalcogen bonds | all 4 units identically oriented, ev [0.05, 0.32, 0.64] |
| c061 | Cs₂S₃ (Cmc2₁) | bent **S₃²⁻** trimers (2.09 Å, ∠109°) | same, ev [0.05, 0.29, 0.66] |
| c038 | Tl₃SbS₃ (R3m) | **SbS₃ pyramids** (2.47 Å) + Tl⁺ 6s² lone pairs, isolated units | pyramid normals **[0,0,1]** — all ∥ c |
| c043/c040 | NaSrBS₃ | **planar BS₃³⁻** π‑triangles (planarity sv₃/sv₁ = 0.000) | normals **[0,0,1]** — perfectly coplanar |
| c069 | Ag₂TeS₃ (Cc) | aligned TeS₃ pyramids (Te⁴⁺ lone pair) + polarizable Ag–S | normals ev 0.97 |

**Reasoning for the winners**

- **c062** is the textbook maximum‑Δn architecture: an isolated *linear*, π‑conjugated triatomic anion with all units strictly parallel, embedded in a weakly polarizable Cs⁺ lattice. This is the NaN₃/BO₂⁻ design principle (Δn ≳ 0.4–0.6), but with far softer P/As π systems → the largest anisotropy in the pool.
- **c089 / c061** are alkali polychalcogenides. Homopolar Se–Se / S–S bonds plus terminal lone pairs give enormous in‑plane vs out‑of‑plane polarizability contrast, and here every Se₃/S₃ unit sits in the same (a,c) plane (almost no bond density along **b**). Se ≫ S in polarizability, so c089 > c061.
- **c038** Tl₃SbS₃ is the Tl₃AsSe₃ (TAS) family — trigonal, all SbS₃ lone‑pair pyramids co‑aligned along *c*, plus stereochemically active Tl⁺; this class is experimentally strongly birefringent (Δn ≈ 0.2).
- **c043** NaSrBS₃: perfectly coplanar planar thioborate triangles — the calcite/BBO mechanism, amplified by S replacing O.

**Rejected:** all zinc‑blende/wurtzite and tetrahedral chalcogenides (SiC polytypes c024–c029, BeSe c037, ZnGa₂S₄, AlCuSe₂, CuAlS₂, Li–Mg/Zn–Ga–Se family, Al₃Ga₃As₆) — isotropic tetrahedra give bond tensors ≈ [⅓,⅓,⅓] and Δn ≲ 0.03; cubic entries (c027, c037, c059, c065, c070, c072) are strictly Δn = 0.

Runners‑up: c069 (Ag₂TeS₃), c040 (= c043 duplicate setting), c064 (Tl₂S₅), c067/c046 (layered ALiZnS₂).

**Final: c062, c089, c061, c038, c043**

def dim(s,tol=1.15):
    # union-find over supercell-free periodic graph with lattice vector accumulation
    N=len(s)
    parent=list(range(N)); off=[np.zeros(3) for _ in range(N)]
    vecs=[]
    def find(i):
        # path with offset
        path=[]
        while parent[i]!=i:
            path.append(i); i=parent[i]
        return i
    def getoff(i):
        o=np.zeros(3)
        while parent[i]!=i:
            o=o+off[i]; i=parent[i]
        return i,o
    for i,si in enumerate(s):
        ri=si.specie.atomic_radius or 1.3
        for n in s.get_neighbors(si,4.6):
            j=n.index
            rj=n.specie.atomic_radius or 1.3
            if n.nn_distance > tol*(ri+rj): continue
            # lattice offset
            fj=s.lattice.get_fractional_coords(n.coords)
            L=np.round(fj - s[j].frac_coords)
            a,oa=getoff(i); b,ob=getoff(j)
            # frac(i) + ... going i->j adds L
            if a==b:
                v=ob - oa + L
                if np.any(np.abs(v)>0.5): vecs.append(v)
            else:
                parent[b]=a; off[b]=oa - ob + L*0 - L*0 + (oa-ob)*0
                off[b]=oa-ob+L*(-1)*0
                off[b]=oa - ob + L*0
                # correct: off_new such that pos_b_global = pos_a + off
                off[b]=oa - ob - L
                off[b]=oa - ob + L
                off[b]= -(oa) + ob + L  # ambiguous; use simple
                off[b]= oa - ob + L
    if not vecs: return 0
    M=np.array(vecs)
    return np.linalg.matrix_rank(M,tol=1e-6)

    d=dim(s)
    sg=SpacegroupAnalyzer(s,symprec=0.1).get_space_group_symbol()
    print(x['candidate_id'],x['formula'].replace(' ',''),sg,'dim',d)

        for n in s.get_neighbors(si,4.8):
